intelligence.human_view: His eye is the scarcest thing in the machine, and spending it is not the waste — spending tokens to imitate it is. A checker that passes 12/12 in bytes while his eye still finds live defects (fix-1d proved it: checker 6/6, his eye still found the defects) is not a gate; it is a rehearsal. The eye walk's real failure is deeper than cost: a seat that only verifies what is there never thinks ahead with him — it never says "we should do this." So the rule changes from capping the walks to stopping them: the staged page goes straight to him, and his eye is the check.
intelligence.simple_view: Shawn looks at the page himself. He is the one who says if it is good. We do not take pictures to check it for him. We put the real page where he can see it. Then he tells us what he thinks.
intelligence.grandma_view: His eye is the check. We stop taking screenshots to judge the page for him. We bring the real page to him, live at the address he opens, and he decides. If a change made it worse, we put back the good one. The page has just two buttons to move — back and forward, nothing more. The legal bar stays small and clean at the bottom — just links to click. And if it is not live yet, we never say it is.
intelligence.naya_view: The staging-card loop failed all afternoon: version after version of the same page, judged as copies, while the live page waited. The moment the build went live at the real address, he could see it for real — and it was the best he had seen. A preview is a copy; only the live page at the address he opens is the thing itself. The order of work follows from that sentence: the Hub done right, the Personal page done right, the agreement done right — each proven on the page he sees — before anything new starts. Rights first, restrictions last — if at all.
